tests.title: Keys are accepted only in the documented shape
given: a scope with room for entries
tests.when: entries are created with keys A, A_1, a1, _A, a 255-character key, an empty key, a 256-character key, 1A, A-B, A.B and A B
then: A, A_1, a1, _A and the 255-character key are accepted
the empty key, the 256-character key and the ones with a leading digit, a hyphen, a dot or a space are refused 400
no entry is written for a refused key
tests.pseudocode: in the entry validation test file, table over the key cases asserting the status and the scope's entry count

tests.title: Keys match case-insensitively for lookup and for uniqueness
given: a scope holding one entry created as MY_KEY
tests.when: it is read, replaced and deleted as my_key and MyKey, and a create names my_key
then: each lookup finds the entry
the create of my_key is refused as a duplicate
the stored key keeps the casing it was created with
tests.pseudocode: in the entry store integration test file: assert patch('my_key').status == 200; assert post([{'key':'my_key'}]).status == 409; assert list()[0].key == 'MY_KEY'

tests.title: A value at the size limit is accepted and one over it is refused
given: a scope with room for entries
tests.when: entries are created and replaced with values of 0, 1, 262144 and 262145 bytes
then: the values up to and including 262144 bytes are accepted
262145 bytes is refused 400 on both create and replace
the stored value is unchanged after a refused replace
tests.pseudocode: in the entry validation test file, table over the four sizes for both create and replace

tests.title: A scope holds at most 100 entries and an over-full create writes none of them
given: a scope holding 98 entries
tests.when: a create of two entries is made, then a create of one, and then a create of three against a scope holding 98
then: the create that brings the scope to exactly 100 succeeds
the next create of one entry is refused 400
the create of three against 98 is refused 400 and writes none of the three, leaving the count at 98
tests.pseudocode: in the entry store integration test file: fill(98); assert post(2).status == 201 and count() == 100; assert post(1).status == 400; reset(98); assert post(3).status == 400 and count() == 98

tests.title: Lists are ordered by key ignoring case
given: a scope holding keys created in the order B_KEY, a_key, C_KEY and A_OTHER
tests.when: the scope is listed
then: the order is a_key, A_OTHER, B_KEY, C_KEY
the same order is produced for both secrets and variables
tests.pseudocode: in the entry store test file: assert [e.key for e in list()] == ['a_key','A_OTHER','B_KEY','C_KEY']

tests.title: Secrets are created at each scope and the response carries no value
given: a user, an organization the user belongs to, and a workspace the user owns
tests.when: a create of two entries is made at each of the three secret scopes
then: each answers 201 with an array of the created entries
every element carries key, created_at and updated_at and no value key
each entry is afterwards present in its own scope and absent from the other two
tests.pseudocode: in the secret routes' integration test file, table over the three scopes: r = post(scope, entries); assert r.status == 201 and all('value' not in e for e in r.json)

tests.title: Secrets are listed, replaced and deleted at each scope without ever returning a value
given: each of the three secret scopes holding two entries
tests.when: the scope is listed, one entry's value is replaced, the entry is read back in a list, and then deleted
then: the list answers 200 with keys and timestamps and no values
the replace answers 200 with the entry and no value, and updates updated_at
the delete answers 204 and the entry is gone from the list
tests.pseudocode: in the secret routes' integration test file, table over the three scopes running the four calls in sequence

tests.title: Each secret scope admits exactly the callers the reference names
given: a user credential, an admin token, a member of the organization, a non-member, a workspace owner, a member of the workspace's organization and a stranger
tests.when: each calls the list route of each of the three secret scopes
then: the admin token is refused 403 on the user scope
a non-member is refused 404 on the organization scope
a member of the workspace's organization and a stranger are both refused 404 on the workspace scope
the owner and an admin token are served the workspace scope
tests.pseudocode: in the secret routes' test file, table over (scope, caller, expectedStatus)

tests.title: A duplicate key refuses the whole create
given: a scope already holding MY_KEY with a known value
tests.when: a create names my_key alone, and then a create names a fresh key and my_key together
then: both answer 409
the existing entry's value and updated_at are unchanged
the fresh key of the second create was not written
tests.pseudocode: in the entry store test file: assert post([{'key':'my_key'}]).status == 409; assert post([fresh, dup]).status == 409 and fresh.key not in keys()

tests.title: Missing values, unknown keys and unreachable scopes are refused
given: a scope holding one entry, an organization slug naming nothing, and a workspace slug naming nothing
tests.when: a replace is called with no value, a replace and a delete name a key the scope lacks, and a list is called for the unknown organization and the unknown workspace
then: the replace with no value answers 400
the unknown key answers 404 on both replace and delete
the unknown organization and workspace answer 404
the scope's entries are unchanged throughout
tests.pseudocode: in the secret routes' test file, table over the five cases asserting status and an unchanged scope

tests.title: Variables are created, listed, replaced and deleted, with their values
given: each of the three variable scopes
tests.when: two entries are created, listed, one replaced and one deleted at each scope
then: create answers 201 and list and replace answer 200, every element carrying key, value, created_at and updated_at
the value returned is the one stored
delete answers 204 and the entry is gone
tests.pseudocode: in the variable routes' integration test file, table over the three scopes running the four calls in sequence

tests.title: Variables obey the same key, size, count and duplicate rules as secrets
given: a variable scope
tests.when: the key, value-size, entry-count and duplicate cases of the secret tests are replayed against the variable routes
then: each answers with the same status as its secret counterpart
no entry is written for any refused case
tests.pseudocode: in the variable routes' test file, reusing the secret rule table against the variable routes and asserting identical statuses

tests.title: A member of the organization reads a workspace's variables as the owner does
given: a workspace with two variables, its owner and a member of its organization
tests.when: both list the workspace's variables
then: both answer 200
the two responses are identical, values included
tests.pseudocode: in the variable routes' integration test file: assert list(owner).json == list(member).json

tests.title: A member cannot change a workspace's variables
given: a workspace with one variable and a member of its organization
tests.when: the member creates, replaces and deletes a workspace variable
then: each answers 403 with error_type forbidden and the documented message
the workspace's variables are unchanged
tests.pseudocode: in the variable routes' test file, table over the three write verbs asserting 403, the error_type and an unchanged scope

tests.title: A variable named like a workspace setting governs nothing
given: a workspace whose settings are at their defaults
tests.when: variables named after each of the twelve settings are created at the workspace scope, with values that would be valid for those settings
then: the workspace's settings object is unchanged
no behaviour the settings control changes
the variables are listed as ordinary variables
tests.pseudocode: in the variable routes' integration test file: for name in SETTING_NAMES: create_var(name, value); assert workspace().settings == DEFAULTS

tests.title: The resolved view merges three tiers and reports each value's origin
given: a workspace whose owner belongs to its organization
a key set at all three tiers, one at the organization and workspace tiers, one only at the organization tier and one only at the workspace tier
tests.when: the resolved view is requested
then: each key appears exactly once
the key set at all three carries the workspace's value and origin workspace
the key set at the organization and workspace tiers carries the workspace's value
the organization-only key carries origin org and the workspace-only key origin workspace
tests.pseudocode: in the resolved view integration test file: r = get(f'/api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/vars/resolved'); assert {e.key: (e.value, e.origin) for e in r.json} == expected

tests.title: The user tier is the workspace owner's, not the caller's
given: a workspace, its owner with a variable at user scope, and a member of its organization with a different variable at their own user scope
tests.when: the owner and the member each read the resolved view
then: the owner's user variable appears with origin user in both answers
the member's own user variable appears in neither
the two answers are identical
tests.pseudocode: in the resolved view integration test file: assert get(resolved, owner).json == get(resolved, member).json and ownerVar in keys and memberVar not in keys

tests.title: The organization tier is skipped when the owner is not a member of it
given: a workspace in an organization whose owner is not a member of that organization, with a variable set at that organization's scope
tests.when: the resolved view is requested
then: the organization's variable does not appear
variables from the owner's user scope and the workspace scope still appear
tests.pseudocode: in the resolved view integration test file: remove_owner_from_org(); assert orgVar not in keys(get(resolved).json)

tests.title: The resolved view is ordered by key ignoring case
given: variables across the three tiers whose keys interleave in case-insensitive order
tests.when: the resolved view is requested
then: the array is in case-insensitive ascending key order
the order does not depend on which tier each value came from
tests.pseudocode: in the resolved view test file: assert [e.key for e in resolved()] == sorted(all_keys, key=str.lower)

tests.title: No secret route returns a value
given: a distinctive value stored as a secret at each of the three scopes
tests.when: the create, list, replace and delete routes of each scope are called and their responses inspected
then: no response body contains the distinctive value
no response body carries a value key at all
the corresponding variable routes do return the value, so the difference is of the kind and not of the serialiser
tests.pseudocode: in the secret routes' test file, table over (scope, route): assert SENTINEL not in response.text and 'value' not in element

tests.title: A stored secret's value is not recoverable from the store
given: a secret written with a distinctive value at each of the three scopes
tests.when: the raw contents of the underlying store are dumped
then: the dump contains no occurrence of any distinctive value
the keys are present in the dump, so the absence of the values is encryption and not a failed write
reading each secret back through the service still yields the original value to the code that uses it
tests.pseudocode: in the secret store integration test file: write(SENTINEL); assert SENTINEL not in raw_dump() and key in raw_dump(); assert store.get(scope, key) == SENTINEL

tests.title: No secret value reaches a log record
given: a recording log sink and a distinctive secret value
tests.when: a create, a replace, a refused create and a request that raises an unhandled failure are made with that value
then: no log record contains the value
the log records do carry the request's route template, so the scrubbing is of the value and not of logging generally
tests.pseudocode: in the secret routes' test file: for scenario in SCENARIOS: run(scenario, value=SENTINEL); assert SENTINEL not in sink.text

tests.title: A workspace secret is stored and never comes back out
given: a running deployment and a workspace owned by the caller
tests.when: a secret with a distinctive value is created in the workspace's scope, the scope is listed, and the store is inspected
then: the create answers 201 with the key and no value
the list shows the key and no value
the raw store holds no occurrence of the value
tests.pseudocode: in the secrets smoke test file: post(workspace secret, SENTINEL); assert 'value' not in list()[0]; assert SENTINEL not in raw_dump()

tests.title: Variables resolve across the three tiers against a running deployment
given: a running deployment, a workspace whose owner belongs to its organization
tests.when: one key is set at the owner's user scope, the organization scope and the workspace scope, a second only at the user scope, and the resolved view is read
then: the first key appears once with the workspace's value and origin workspace
the second appears with origin user
the array is ordered by key ignoring case
tests.pseudocode: in the variables smoke test file: set three tiers; r = get(resolved); assert r.json matches the expected (value, origin) pairs

tests.title: A member reads a workspace's variables and is refused its writes and its secrets
given: a running deployment, a workspace with variables and secrets, and a member of its organization
tests.when: the member lists the variables, creates one, and lists the secrets
then: the variable list answers 200 with values
the variable create answers 403 with error_type forbidden
the secret list answers 404
tests.pseudocode: in the variables smoke test file: assert list_vars(member).status == 200 and create_var(member).json.error.error_type == 'forbidden' and list_secrets(member).status == 404
